newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil extra sugar exports set at 500,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil extra sugar exports set at 500,000 tonnes.

text.p: Extra sugar exports authorized by Brazil's government total 500,000 tonnes, a Ministry of Industry and Commerce official said Wednesday.

The official in the sugar and alcohol department said a decree published in December allocated an extra 400,000 tonnes of exports to the centre south plus 100,000 tonnes to two mills which had been left out of the original 1996/97 sugar crop plan.
The decree included 52,318 tonnes for the north-northeast but the official said this involved a quota swap between mills and did not represent additional exports.
"The total is exactly 500,000 tonnes," the official said, clarifying some confusion over the additional quota.

Sugar and alcohol department head Pedro Cabral told Reuters earlier this week that tax exemption for the extra exports was awaiting the signature of Finance Minister Pedro Malan and a decree was likely to be published soon.

Traders note that the additional export quota will have little immediate effect because most mills have no produce left to ship. They say they are likely to either sell their quotas to other mills or use them for the next crop.
